paragraphs.zh: In a 1 I stirred apparatus, 100g of 2-chloro-3-methyl4-sulfonylmethylbenzoic acid were suspended in 400 ml of chlorobenzene. At room temperature, 85.9 g of N-bromosuccinimide and 6.6 g of azoisobutyroniltrile were added and the mixture was subsequently heated to 60° C. Afterwards, 2.6 g of bromine were added and the reaction mixture was further heated gradually to 90° C. The mixture was stirred at 90° C. for 2 h; after this time, HPLC analysis indicated a conversion of more than 98%. After the reaction mixture had been cooled, 100 ml of a 2% sodium bisulfite solution and 400 ml of water were added in succession and stirred well. The suspension was filtered, and the solid was washed and dried at 60° C. under reduced pressure.
paragraphs.en: In a 1 l (one litre) stirred apparatus, 100 g of 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-(methylsulfonyl)benzoic acid were suspended in 400 ml of chlorobenzene. At room temperature, 85.9 g of N-bromosuccinimide and 6.6 g of azoisobutyronitrile were added and the mixture was subsequently heated to 60° C. Afterwards, 2.6 g of bromine were added and the reaction mixture was further heated gradually to 90° C. The mixture was stirred at 90° C. for 2 h; after this time, HPLC analysis indicated a conversion of more than 98%. After the reaction mixture had been cooled, 100 ml of a 2% sodium bisulfite solution and 400 ml of water were added in succession and stirred well. The suspension was filtered, and the solid was washed and dried at 60° C. under reduced pressure.
paragraphs.notes: Four things read off the pixels at 6x to 8x magnification, all verified glyph by glyph. (1) The vessel size is printed '1 I': a digit one, a space, then a CAPITAL I with full top and bottom serifs, plainly not the lowercase l used in 'ml' and 'chlorobenzene' two lines below and not a second digit one. It is the litre symbol set as a capital I in the published typesetting; en gives it as '1 l'. (2) '100g' is printed CLOSED UP, with no space between the number and the g, unlike every other quantity on the page ('85.9 g', '6.6 g', '2.6 g'). (3) The starting material is printed '2-chloro-3-methyl4-sulfonylmethylbenzoic acid': no hyphen between 'methyl' and '4', and the substituent written as 'sulfonylmethyl' rather than 'methylsulfonyl'. Recorded as printed; the chemistry mismatch is in discrepancies. (4) The initiator is printed 'azoisobutyroniltrile' - a-z-o-i-s-o-b-u-t-y-r-o-n-i-l-t-r-i-l-e, with an l between the n-i and the t. Claim 7 on this same page spells it correctly as 'azoisobutyronitrile'. en gives the correct spelling. Everything else matches: 400 ml chlorobenzene, 85.9 g NBS, 6.6 g initiator, 2.6 g bromine, 60° C then 90° C, 2 h, more than 98% conversion, 100 ml of 2% sodium bisulfite, 400 ml water, dried at 60° C. 'N-bro-mosuccinimide' is broken across a line; the soft hyphen has been closed up and the printed spelling there does carry the second n.

paragraphs.zh: A 250 ml glass flask was initially charged with 5 g of 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-sulfonylmethylbenzoic acid in 50 ml of methylene chloride and 50 ml of water. Under irradiation with a 300 W lamp, II g of bromine were gradually metered in over 3 h, and the mixture boiled under reflux. After a further 2 h of irradiation, the reaction mixture had been substantially decolorized. According to HPLC analysis, the reaction mixture contained 87% of product and 10% of reactant.

Under irradiation with a 300 W lamp, [II] g of bromine were gradually metered in over 3 h, and the mixture boiled under reflux. After a further 2 h of irradiation, the reaction mixture had been substantially decolorized. According to HPLC analysis, the reaction mixture contained 87% of product and 10% of reactant.
paragraphs.notes: THE BROMINE CHARGE IS NOT A READABLE NUMBER. Examined at 8x: the page prints two adjacent CAPITAL I glyphs, narrow uprights with symmetric full-width serifs top and bottom. They are not digit ones - the digit 1 elsewhere on this page ('121.3', '100g', '150', '103') has a diagonal top flag and a wider foot, and neither is present. So the page literally prints 'II g of bromine'. The intended value is almost certainly 11 g but the pixels do not say so, and it is NOT written out anywhere else on the page, so it is left as printed and NOT corrected. Any downstream mass balance on Example 1 variant B must treat this quantity as unresolved. Everything else confirmed exactly: 5 g starting material, 250 ml glass flask, 50 ml methylene chloride, 50 ml water, 300 W lamp, 3 h metering, further 2 h irradiation, 87% product, 10% reactant. paragraphs.zh: In a 0.5 I stirred apparatus, 20 g of 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-sulfonylethylbenzoic acid were suspended in 150 ml of acetonitrile. At room temperature, 17.6 g of N-bromosuccinimide and 0.7 g of dibenzoyl peroxide were added and the mixture was subsequently heated to reflux. After in each case 1 h, further dibenzoyl peroxide was added in 3 portions each of 0.7 g and the mixture was stirred for a further 2 h after the last addition. After this time, HPLC analysis indicated complete conversion. After the reaction mixture had been cooled, 100 ml of a 2% sodium bisulfite solution and 300 ml of ethyl acetate were added in succession. The organic phase was removed, washed and concentrated under reduced pressure. The solid residue was suspended in 50 ml of diethyl ether and 20 ml of heptane, filtered off and dried. 28.2 g (95.6% of theory) of 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro-4-ethylsulfonylbenzoic acid were obtained.
paragraphs.en: In a 0.5 l (half litre) stirred apparatus, 20 g of 2-chloro-3-methyl-4-(ethylsulfonyl)benzoic acid were suspended in 150 ml of acetonitrile. At room temperature, 17.6 g of N-bromosuccinimide and 0.7 g of dibenzoyl peroxide were added and the mixture was subsequently heated to reflux. After in each case 1 h, further dibenzoyl peroxide was added in 3 portions each of 0.7 g and the mixture was stirred for a further 2 h after the last addition. After this time, HPLC analysis indicated complete conversion. After the reaction mixture had been cooled, 100 ml of a 2% sodium bisulfite solution and 300 ml of ethyl acetate were added in succession. The organic phase was removed, washed and concentrated under reduced pressure. The solid residue was suspended in 50 ml of diethyl ether and 20 ml of heptane, filtered off and dried. 28.2 g (95.6% of theory) of 3-bromomethyl-2-chloro-4-ethylsulfonylbenzoic acid were obtained.
paragraphs.notes: Read at 3x and the numbers spot-checked at 7x. The vessel size is printed '0.5 I' with the same CAPITAL I glyph as [0027], here at normal weight; en gives '0.5 l'. 'stirred' is lowercase s as printed. The starting material is printed '2-chloro-3-methyl-4-sulfonylethylbenzoic acid', i.e. 'sulfonylethyl' the wrong way round, while the title three lines above prints 'ethylsulfonyl'; recorded as printed, see discrepancies. Every quantity confirmed against the pixels and every one matches: 20 g starting material, 150 ml acetonitrile, 17.6 g N-bromosuccinimide, 0.7 g dibenzoyl peroxide initially, 3 further portions of 0.7 g each added after 1 h in each case, 2 h further stirring, 100 ml of 2% sodium bisulfite, 300 ml ethyl acetate, 50 ml diethyl ether, 20 ml heptane, 28.2 g, 95.6% of theory. The yield is self-consistent once the 88% purity of [0034] is applied: 28.2 g x 0.88 = 24.8 g of pure C10H10BrClO4S (341.6) = 0.0727 mol, which is 95.4% of the 0.0761 mol charged as 20 g of C10H11ClO4S (262.7). Uncorrected it would exceed 100%, so the stated yield is purity-corrected, as in [0028]. 'N-bro-mosuccinimide' is again broken across a line and closed up here; the printed spelling carries the second n.

discrepancies.what: Both examples name the starting material with the sulfone substituent written backwards relative to the drawn formula, the example titles and the rest of the patent.
discrepancies.drawing_says: Formulae (I) and (II) both draw SO2R2 attached to C4 through sulfur, with R2 an alkyl group carried on that sulfur. With R2 = CH3 that group is methylsulfonyl (CH3-SO2-); with R2 = C2H5 it is ethylsulfonyl (C2H5-SO2-).
discrepancies.text_says: [0027] prints '2-chloro-3-methyl4-sulfonylmethylbenzoic acid', [0031] prints '2-chloro-3-methyl-4-sulfonylmethylbenzoic acid' and [0033] prints '2-chloro-3-methyl-4-sulfonylethylbenzoic acid'. 'sulfonylmethyl' and 'sulfonylethyl' name a divalent -SO2-CH2- / -SO2-C2H4- linker, which cannot be a terminal ring substituent, so these are transpositions of 'methylsulfonyl' and 'ethylsulfonyl'. The Example 1 title ('4-methylsulfonylbenzoic'), the Example 2 title ('4-ethylsulfonylbenzoic'), [0020], [0024] and [0028] all use the correct order. Left exactly as printed in every zh field; corrected only in en, and flagged here rather than fixed silently.

[0027] and [0033] both print '100 ml of a 2% sodium bisulfite solution'. Sodium bisulfite is the reagent that makes chemical sense for quenching residual bromine, but the general description as printed says bisulfate. Both readings are recorded as printed.
